02 / Football

A game I grew up with.

I have loved playing football since I was a child, inspired by watching players pull off dazzling skills on the pitch. Growing up, I even dreamed of becoming a professional footballer. I took the sport seriously from an early age, playing about once a week and up to three or four times whenever I had free time. Whenever I had a spare moment, football was on my mind, and I would practise on my own.

My earliest achievements were a Silver Medal and a Bronze Medal in VietGoal tournaments organised by youth football academies. As I grew older, I continued training and playing with middle school and high school friends who shared my passion. The reward I had hoped for finally arrived when our team won the HSGS Cup, our school-wide high school tournament.

03 / Basketball

Finding a new team.

I had never played basketball in elementary or middle school. When I entered high school, its strong basketball community inspired me to start. I began practising, watching tutorials to improve my technique, and learning the rules.

I was selected for my class basketball team and had the chance to represent my class and school in tournaments. Along the way, I met new friends and learned how to adapt to an unfamiliar environment and train with greater dedication. Those lessons have stayed with me beyond the court.

04 / Karate

Learning to keep showing up.

Truthfully, I did not enjoy martial arts when I was younger. On hot summer mornings in Hanoi, I would much rather have stayed in an air-conditioned room with my LEGO toys. Training meant running laps, warming up, and working through the heat. Winter mornings were a different challenge: leaving a warm blanket to run and practise in the cold was rarely appealing.

Over time, I began to understand what those sessions gave me beyond fitness and self-defence. They built endurance in my willpower as well as my body. Keeping a regular sleep schedule, waking up early, and showing up in difficult weather taught me discipline and consistency. The older I get, the more grateful I am that my parents encouraged me to keep training.
